results.evidence: Blake Herrington's 2012 ascent write-up says the route was established as grade VI 5.12b; Nathan Hadley's 2017 trip report (also posted on CascadeClimbers) titles it VI 5.12b, and Climbing.com calls it VI 5.12b. Mountain Project alone lists Grade V. The FA grade VI is adopted, matching alpine_grade and the fa field.

Herrington's write-up gives 14 pitches total with the last anchor at the edge of the woods on pitch 14; Mountain Project's pitch-by-pitch description runs pitches 1-14 (its header says 20). The row's own pitches, pitch_detail and beta use 14, so the itinerary's '20-pitch' is changed to match.

results.correct_value: Pitch 11 (5.12 roof) is the crux; pitch 5 was graded 5.11c but its original line felt harder before part of it fell away
results.evidence: Mountain Project and Hadley's 2020 modernization write-up both name pitch 11, the 5.12 pitch out the huge roof, as the crux. Herrington (2012) felt pitch 5 ('5.11c') was techy 5.12+, but Hadley reports a large part of pitch 5 has since fallen off and is climbed around; pitch_detail now grades it 5.11-. pro_tips[0] reworded so it no longer calls pitch 5 the crux.

patches.find: Pitch 5 is the crux at 5.12+ (graded 5.11c on FA, but climbers report it as significantly harder).
patches.replace: Pitch 11, a 5.12 boulder problem out the big roof, is the crux. Pitch 5 is graded 5.11c, and its original line felt far harder before part of it fell away.

results.correct_value: The collapsed section is on pitch 5; the 2020 reroute higher up avoids the loose 'death flake'
results.evidence: Hadley's 2020 write-up says a whole part of pitch 5 had fallen off, taking bolts with it, and separately that the route was rerouted to avoid the death flake higher on the route. Mountain Project places the old death-flake anchor on pitch 10. pro_tips[1] now places the collapse on pitch 5 and the reroute at the flake.

patches.find: The collapsed roof section on pitch 9/10 (rerouted in 2020) demonstrates route changes since FA
patches.replace: The partly collapsed roof on pitch 5, and the 2020 reroute around a loose flake higher up, show how the route has changed since the FA

results.fact: approach distance to the tower base
results.evidence: Mountain Project and Herrington describe the approach as ~1 mile on the Barclay Creek trail to the bridge, then off-trail up the wash, forested rib and ~800 ft of roped slab (3-3.5 hr), but no source gives a total mileage. The row's waypoint chain routes via Barclay Lake (2.2 mi), which the approach leaves the trail before reaching, so the 3.8 mi figure is doubtful too; straight-line trailhead-to-tower is ~1.4 mi. No two sources give a distance.
